title: indigo_mount_nexstaraux: MOUNT_STATE slew light shows ALERT only on a slew failure, not for a kept coordinates ALERT
description: Audit in 1078b2c4: the light becomes ALERT only when a slew fails. Owner's rule (decided 2026-11-22 for mount_synscan, ticket 1078b2c4, and extended to this driver on 2026-11-23): whenever MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES is in ALERT, the SLEW light of MOUNT_STATE is ALERT too; BUSY while the coordinates are BUSY; otherwise as before. The library keeps a coordinates ALERT until the next BUSY (indigo_update_coordinates() kept-ALERT rule, indigo_reject_coordinates_change()), so the light must be derived from the coordinates state after indigo_update_coordinates() has decided it, at every place the driver publishes the coordinates or MOUNT_STATE (poll, refusals, sync, abort, park/home, connect), not from the driver's own motion flags alone. Reference implementation: synscan_update_mount_state() and its call order in indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver (commit 5f794cc15). Scope: the .driver source (version bump, regenerate with the unchanged generator), simulator-backed cases proving the light follows the coordinates state through a refused/failed request (ALERT kept while idle), the next accepted request (BUSY, then OK/IDLE) and connect, adaptation of existing cases that asserted IDLE under a kept ALERT, recorded run with tools/run_driver_test.py, MIGRATION_STATUS count. Refusals inserted by the generator (parked/homing guards) cannot call driver code; if the light lags there until the next poll, record it in the ticket note and do not change the generator.

outcome.summary: No required changes. Every coordinates publication in the driver is followed by deriving the light; generated files byte-identical to regeneration; abort/parked_guards/reconnect cases rerun by the reviewer, pass; gate in abort_cancels_a_queued_goto deterministic. Non-blocking: header comment of nexstaraux_update_slew_light should mention the on_change exception (called before the generated coordinates publication); MOUNT_STATE is seen just before the coordinates on that path; coordinates published by library code only (geographic coordinates, alignment mode/points) and generator parked guards leave the light out of step until the next poll (<=1 s); suite filters with NEXSTARAUX_TEST_FILTER, not INDIGO_TEST_CASE_FILTER. Not verified: Linux, Windows, hardware.

history.text: Deriving the SLEW light from the coordinates state in the .driver
Writing SLEW light cases in test_mount_nexstaraux_simulator.c
Running filtered nexstaraux cases for the SLEW light
Showing the new SLEW light checks fail against the unfixed driver

Cause: the driver set MOUNT_STATE.SLEW only from its own motion flags (BUSY on goto/park start, ALERT on slew failure/stop, IDLE on arrival) and the poll published MOUNT_STATE before indigo_update_coordinates(). A goto or sync the controller refused, a refused parked request, an abort of a queued goto and a failed poll left MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES ALERT (kept by the library) with the light IDLE; a failed goto's ALERT light also survived a reconnect although the coordinates are defined OK.
Fix (indigo_mount_nexstaraux.driver 28 -> 29, regenerated .c with the unchanged generator; .h/_main.c unchanged): new nexstaraux_update_slew_light() derives the light from the coordinates state (ALERT/BUSY as is, otherwise IDLE). Called after indigo_update_coordinates() in the poll (MOUNT_STATE now published after the coordinates) and its failed-read branch, mount_slew_failed(), the finalizer's stop and arrival paths (replacing the hand-set ALERT/IDLE), the abort of a queued request (plus MOUNT_STATE update), on_connect (light defined with the coordinates), and at the end of the MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES on_change for a non-BUSY result: the generator appends indigo_update_coordinates() after on_change, and since the admitted BUSY cleared the kept ALERT that result is published unchanged, so MOUNT_STATE is published just ahead of it. Goto/park start still set BUSY explicitly.
Generator-inserted refusals (parked guard in change_property and in the handler) run no driver code: the light follows at the next poll (<= 1 s idle); recorded as accepted lag, generator not changed.
Tests (test_mount_nexstaraux_simulator.c): slew_command_failure (refused goto: coordinates+light ALERT over 3 polls; next goto shows the light BUSY, ends OK/IDLE), sync_command_failure (refused sync ALERT over polls; accepted sync IDLE), parked_guards (parked GOTO and sync refusals ALERT over polls, still ALERT after unpark, BUSY at the accepted goto), reconnect (refused goto, reconnect: MOUNT_STATE defined

No existing case asserted IDLE under a kept ALERT; mount_state_lights passes unchanged.
Without the fix (HEAD driver rebuilt): slew_command_failure, sync_command_failure, parked_guards fail with 'after poll 0 the coordinates are 3 and the SLEW light 0'; abort_cancels_a_queued_goto fails (no SLEW ALERT publication); reconnect fails (light never ALERT). With the fix minus only the on_connect line, reconnect fails with MOUNT_STATE defined with SLEW 3 (expected 0).
Recorded run: python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_nexstaraux -> 2026-11-23 16:01 3.0.0.29 mac arm64 simulator 71/71 OK. MIGRATION_STATUS count 70 -> 71 (HW count unchanged). flow check whitespace passed.
Not verified: Linux, Windows, hardware (no hardware run).
